recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中，有幾顆紅血球（含一顆偏多染性者）細胞質內散布著明顯的藍紫色粗大點狀顆粒（coarse basophilic stippling），其餘紅血球大致正常，這種粗點彩在鉛中毒時很典型。
features: Red cells containing coarse, dark blue-purple punctate granules distributed through the cytoplasm (coarse basophilic stippling)
Stippled cells are slightly polychromatic and similar in size to neighboring red cells
Occasional poikilocytes including fragments, an elongated cell, and a stomatocyte-like cell
Most red cells are normochromic with central pallor
Scattered platelets; no leukocytes in the field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a mostly normochromic red cell population with scattered cells exhibiting coarse basophilic stippling, seen as numerous dark blue punctate granules distributed through the cytoplasm of slightly polychromatic erythrocytes. Mild poikilocytosis with occasional fragments and elongated forms is present. No nucleated red cells or abnormal leukocytes are seen in this field. Coarse basophilic stippling, reflecting aggregated ribosomal RNA from pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase inhibition, is suggestive of lead poisoning in the appropriate clinical setting; blood lead level measurement is recommended.

ddx.vs: Thalassemia also shows basophilic stippling but with pronounced microcytosis, hypochromia, and target cells on a background of otherwise abnormal indices.
Hereditary P5'N deficiency produces identical stippling and hemolysis but with normal blood lead and a congenital history.
Pappenheimer bodies are fewer, small clustered granules at the cell periphery that stain with Prussian blue, rather than evenly dispersed iron-negative stippling.
Precipitate lies on top of cells and in the background in variable focal planes rather than being confined within individual erythrocytes.
